title: Cabin-Flex Rear Galley Complex and Deep Stowage Arrangement for ZEPHYR-24 Evo Aircraft
abstract: Rearrangement of the rear galley complex and introduction of pivoting deep stowage compartments on the ZEPHYR-24 Evo, releasing two seat rows of floor area and raising carry-on capacity to one bag per passenger.

sections.reason: The ZEPHYR-24 Evo cabin was selling into markets where the carry-on allowance is one full-size bag per passenger, and the original stowage volume forced gate-checking on about one flight in three at typical load factors. Operators were also asking for the two seat rows released by moving the rear galley complex against the rear pressure bulkhead. The change is entirely commercial: there is no in-service issue with the previous arrangement, and the two configurations continue in parallel because not every customer wants the denser layout.
sections.description: The rear galley complex is repositioned aft and the door 4 area is re-arranged so that two additional seat rows fit into the released floor area. The overhead stowage is replaced by pivoting deep compartments using the trim kit D2520122039443, the curtain rail D2520125397271 and the revised lining D2520123607135, with cushioned clamps AES113070-9A carrying the gas strut anchorage. The obsolete monument fitting D2520125508153 is deleted and the bin load is taken directly into the frame tie. The stowage FINs 6DL3 and 8010DQ6 change position and the decor panel FIN 5138DL is re-profiled at the lower edge to clear the pivoting bin in the open position. Work is in zones 272, 981 and 984 with the rear cabin stripped. Drawing D25201287724 issue A carries the bin envelope and the frame tie interface.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 74 kg per aircraft including the additional seats, distributed aft of the centre of gravity, giving a shift of 0.31 per cent MAC that the weight and balance manual will reflect. Electrical load increases by 340 VA for the additional lighting and service units. The deep stowage is not interchangeable with the previous bin because the frame tie interface differs. Emergency egress from the rear cabin has to be re-demonstrated with the additional rows, and the passenger service unit distribution is being re-certified. AMM, IPC and cabin definition content for ATA 25-20 and 25-30 will be extensively re-issued.
sections.embodiment_note: Planned as a customer option with a production cut-in still to be confirmed, followed by a rear cabin conversion bulletin for the in-service fleet. Conversion is expected to take about twelve days with the rear cabin stripped and will be offered only alongside a cabin refresh.

type_data.balance_impact: Aft mass addition, CG shift 0.31 % MAC, weight and balance manual updated
type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN Z11660 as a customer option; both cabin arrangements remain in production
